plan.summary: BRO-4623 part 7: remove capitalization figures and recoupment dates for The Lion King and Aladdin that had no citable source (Disney does not disclose either), fix Boop's capitalization attribution and leftover merge text, use the reported 'up to $18M' for Cats: The Jellicle Ball and fix its venue note, remove Oedipus' unsourced figure and wrong closing date, update Chess' stale note, and drop a non-public staging URL from Here There Are Blueberries.
steps: The Lion King / Aladdin: Disney never announces capitalization or recoupment (Broadway Journal, May 2023: a Disney rep declined to comment on finances). Recouped status stays (Lion King $2B+ gross; Aladdin $561M+ by May 2023) but the figures go and the source lines say the dates are estimates. Aladdin's date drops to year precision.
Boop: Variety and Deadline (Jun 2025) reported up to $26M; a July 2025 SEC Form D/A raised the maximum to $29M. The source line now says both.

Cats: The Jellicle Ball: The Hollywood Reporter: 'capitalized for up to $18 million, according to securities filings'; transferred from PAC NYC to the Broadhurst, closed Aug 8, 2026 after winning three Tonys.
Oedipus: final performance Feb 8, 2026 with a Studio 54 house record of $1,212,949 (Playbill). The $6.5M figure came from an AI research pass, not a cited filing.
Chess: closed early Jun 21, 2026 (Variety); producers said it will not recoup (Deadline, May 26, 2026). $15M per SEC Form D/A (Chess Champion LLC, Jan 5, 2026).

actions.oldValue: Disney sole-funded production — no outside investors. Disney never announces recoupments: per insider, 'recoupment is not a concept that makes sense in the Disney model' since they handle many services in-house (marketing, ticketing, merchandise). $15-17M cap (Disney won't confirm). Recouped likely late 2014. Weekly nut ~$850K. Disney's unique New Amsterdam Theatre lease pays 2% of gross as rent (vs standard fixed rent of $50-100K/week), confirmed by GPT DR. Received $3M NY theater tax credit (2022-2023 fiscal year). By May 2023: $561M+ grossed, 3,100+ performances. NOT eligible for SVOG (Disney is a publicly traded company, per Variety Mar 2021). Multiple international productions. One of the most profitable Broadway shows of the 2010s.
actions.newValue: Disney Theatrical production, funded entirely by Disney with no outside investors. Disney does not disclose capitalization or announce recoupments. Received a $3M NY State theater tax credit (2022-23). Had grossed over $561M across 3,100+ performances by May 2023 (Broadway Journal). Not eligible for SVOG because Disney is publicly traded (Variety, Mar 2021).

actions.oldValue: Capitalized at $29M (SEC D/A, up from $26M). Closed July 13, 2025 after 112 performances. Weekly nut ~$750K but previews grossed only ~$530K (weekly loss ~$300K). Rarely grossed above $700K — consistently below breakeven. Investors lost ~80-100% of capital. David Foster composed. Jerry Mitchell directed/choreographed. William Haber / Ostar Enterprises. c/o Foresight Theatrical. Low ATP (~$70 previews) from heavy discounting for family audiences. [Merged from duplicate boop-2025 entry: Closed after 112 performances, lost entire $26 million investment. Part of broader Broadway crisis where none of 18 new musicals from 2025 season made profit.]
actions.newValue: New musical directed and choreographed by Jerry Mitchell, music by David Foster. Closed Jul 13, 2025 after 112 performances without recouping (Variety, Deadline).
